diffs.diff: header pin 1: part says VIN, datasheet reading says Vin+
diffs.evidence: Adafruit INA219 STEMMA QT breakout (product 904) top silkscreen, 6-pin header left to right reads: VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, VIN-, VIN+ (the part's order). The second reading listed the pin names from the Adafruit guide text (Vin+/Vin- screw-terminal pins, VCC) in an arbitrary order, not the header order; the guide calls the power pin 'VIN - This is the power pin', i.e. the reading's 'VCC'. Header position 1 is silkscreened 'VIN'.

diffs.diff: shunt_voltage_V: datasheet reading gives 0.00001 per count, the part's model has 0.004, 0.1
diffs.evidence: TI INA219 datasheet: 'Shunt voltage, 1 LSB step size 10 uV' and 'Bus voltage, 1 LSB step size 4 mV'. The model agrees in different units: 0.004 is the bus-voltage scale (V/count, after >>3); 0.1 is the shunt register expressed as load current in mA/count = 10 uV / 0.1 ohm (R100 shunt on the board). The driver uses raw*0.01 mV (=10 uV) for shunt_mv().
